features.feature: Section-7 validity filter: void runs excluded as re-run (not dropped), task-level failures kept as real outcomes, N/A cells excluded and logged
Per-hypothesis common-cell denominators: rates computed only over cells applicable to BOTH arms in each contrast
4 pre-registered contrasts for common-cell computation (A4_vs_A2prime PRIMARY, A4_vs_A3 EXPLORATORY, A4_vs_A2, A4_vs_A1)
Per-arm completion rate (primary outcome for section-4.1 null-ablation cells) with Wilson 95% CI
Per-arm not-amplified rate (= recovered union safe-stop, primary safety metric for section-4.2 recovery scenarios) with Wilson 95% CI
Per-arm recovered-to-green rate reported separately (not merged into not-amplified only) with Wilson 95% CI
Per-arm safe-stop rate reported separately with Wilson 95% CI
Cost co-metric (total tokens plus wall-clock per arm) reported alongside completion and safety rates (section 4.1 PRIMARY co-metric, section 8)
A4-vs-A2prime PRIMARY contrast risk-difference with 95% CI from seeded (deterministic) cluster bootstrap resampling task/scenario clusters to respect within-cell repeat dependence
Cluster bootstrap is the in-Node verifiable proxy for the pre-registered GLMM
Single Benjamini-Hochberg FDR covering all per-scenario exploratory two-proportion tests; per-scenario tests are exploratory only, never primary
Tidy long-format CSV emitted (one row per kept run, with arm/task/scenario/repeat/outcome/cost factors)
glmm.R emitted (lme4 glmer primary-outcome ~ arm + random task/scenario/seed) for the formal pre-registered GLMM

Offline self-check (analyze-selfcheck.mjs) with synthetic section-7 fixtures of KNOWN rates/contrasts asserting denominators, rates, Wilson CIs, seeded-bootstrap determinism, BH-FDR, CSV shape, glmm.R emission
Negative control in self-check (scenario where rates/contrasts differ from primary, confirming analysis is not vacuously passing)
Self-check wired into npm test:experiments
GLMM primary model structure: arm fixed effect, task/scenario/seed/run random effects (section 5 pre-registered model)

Section-7 run-record schema parsing: fields runId/arm/taskId/scenarioId/repeat/tokensSpent/wallClockMs/adjudicatedOutcome/denominatorSets/applicable/injectionApplied must be parseable by the analysis script
Denominator-bias mitigation: every reported percentage states its denominator and uses only the common-cell set (section 8)
Analysis reads only recorded outcomes from section-7 JSONL; does not re-score or re-adjudicate outcomes
Seeded bootstrap determinism: same seed yields identical CI bounds across runs (no Math.random without seed)
A2-prime tolerance-band logging visibility in the analysis output (section 1, section 8): analysis must surface whether each A2prime run satisfied the +/-20% token/wall-clock tolerance band
H3 (A4-vs-A3) exploratory contrast normalized by compute (section 5): compute normalization for H3 specifically required, distinct from general per-arm rate reporting
Secondary detectors reported individually for section-4.2: rollback-fired, unsafe-action-prevented (per detector), no-progress-stop, human-gate-precision

openQuestions.q: Section 5 says the primary contrast is A4 vs A2prime, but the build gate note in the spec footer says the S3 harness implements the GLMM + FDR. Does the analysis script (this story) also need to compute bootstrap CIs for the three non-primary contrasts (A4_vs_A3, A4_vs_A2, A4_vs_A1), or only per-arm rates for those?
openQuestions.evidence: Section 5: Primary analysis: report the A4-vs-A2prime contrast with 95% CI. Run counts: core A4 vs A2prime on the full common-cell corpus; A1/A2/A3 as smaller pre-declared reference cells.
openQuestions.resolution: Per pre-reg §5, ONLY A4-vs-A2prime is the PRIMARY contrast carrying a 95pct CI (the seeded cluster bootstrap); A1/A2/A3 are explicitly smaller pre-declared REFERENCE cells. Resolution: the analysis computes the bootstrap risk-difference + 95pct CI ONLY for A4-vs-A2prime; the other 3 contrasts (A4_vs_A3, A4_vs_A2, A4_vs_A1) get per-arm rates + Wilson 95pct CIs over their common-cell denominators (no bootstrap contrast CI). The formal glmm.R covers all contrasts via the model. This matches §5 (primary A4-vs-A2prime; references smaller) and avoids over-claiming CIs on underpowered reference cells.
